title: Longest Palindrome After Substring Concatenation I
summary: Given strings s and t, determine the maximum length of a palindrome formed by concatenating a substring from s with a substring from t.
statement: Given strings s and t, determine the maximum length of a palindrome formed by concatenating a substring from s with a substring from t.
constraints: s and t are nonempty lowercase strings.
Choose a contiguous substring from s and one from t; either may be empty; concatenate them in that order.
Return the maximum possible palindrome length.
hints: A cross-string palindrome has matching outer pieces from s and reversed t, plus an optional palindrome center from either string.
Precompute the longest palindrome starting at every position, then build common-suffix lengths between s and reversed t.
For each matching DP cell, double the paired length and append the best available center immediately afterward on either side.
Every concatenated palindrome decomposes into equal mirrored cross-string arms and at most one within-string center, all represented by these states.
editorial: Every concatenated palindrome decomposes into equal mirrored cross-string arms and at most one within-string center, all represented by these states.

tests.explanation: Taking both single letters produces aa of length two.
No cross-string match exists, but a one-letter substring is palindromic.
